title: Tunisian cable stitch headband
excerpt: A stretchy headband with a faux-cable running down the centre, worked in DK yarn on a Tunisian hook. The cables are formed by crossing stitches on the forward pass.
sourceNotes: Tunisian cable stitch crosses groups of vertical bars over each other on the forward pass to mimic knitted cable panels.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crossing technique worked on the forward pass by skipping bars, working the skipped bars, then returning to pick up the skipped ones. This creates a twist that resembles a cable.
Skip the next 2 bars, pick up the following 2 bars, then go back and pick up the 2 skipped bars. Produces a right-leaning cable twist.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 sts x 15 rows = 10 cm in Tunisian simple stitch on 4.0 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 8 cm wide x 50 cm long (to fit most adults).

content.text: on a plain Tunisian simple stitch background. The cable crosses every 4 rows using a
Chain 16. Row 1 forward pass: pick up 15 loops plus edge (16 loops). Return pass: ch 1, work off 2 loops to end.

Work 4 sts in Tunisian simple stitch, then on cable rows cross right over the next 4 sts, then work 4 sts in simple stitch to the edge. Rows 1 to 3: simple stitch throughout. Row 4 (cable row): simple stitch 4, cross right over next 4 bars, simple stitch 4 to end. Repeat this 4-row sequence.
Continue until the headband measures 50 cm. Bind off with slip stitch across. Fold so the cast-on and bind-off edges align, then sew the ends together with the tapestry needle. Weave in all ends.
